entries.title: Job 16:5
segments: Those who have themselves suffered great afflictions, are most disposed and best prepared to sympathize with the afflictions and assuage the grief of others.

entries.title: Job 16:9
segments: In the depths of distress, even good men, if left to themselves, will have hard thoughts, and complain not only of men but of God, and speak as if he not only were the author of their afflictions, but had become their enemy.

entries.title: Job 16:10
segments:
They; Job's pretended friends. 
 
  Smitten me; they had opposed and reproached him.

entries.title: Job 16:11
segments: Whoever may be the instruments of affliction to the people of God, they should not overlook his all-controlling hand, or feel that without his permission others could have any power over them.

entries.title: Job 16:12
segments: Was at ease; before his afflictions came.

entries.title: Job 16:13
segments: He poureth out my gall; an expression denoting the most intense anguish.

entries.title: Job 16:15
segments: Defiled my horn; the horn was an emblem of power, authority, and influence; and the meaning is, he was shorn of his power, his authority was gone.

entries.title: Job 16:17
segments: Pure; free from hypocrisy.  Of this Satan had accused him before God, and his friends had insinuated against him the same charge.

entries.title: Job 16:18
segments:
Cover not thou my blood; he speaks of himself as an innocent man appointed to die, and asks the earth to leave his blood uncovered that it may cry aloud for redress. 
 
  Let my cry have no place; that is, the cry of my blood: let it have no place where it shall be hid in silence.  According to others the meaning is, that if he had been guilty of heaven-daring crimes as his enemies charged, he did not ask that his crime should be hid; nor could he expect that God would hear his cry for deliverance from punishment.

entries.title: Job 16:19
segments: My witness is in heaven; God knows that I am sincere, though here I am charged with hypocrisy.

entries.title: Job 16:20
segments: When the soul pours out its complaints to God, and looks to him for help, though he may not at once seem to hear, in due time he will answer and grant a glorious deliverance.

entries.title: Job 16:22
segments: When a few years are come; if he is to have any deliverance in this life, it must come speedily, for death is near.
